n: Mature cystic teratoma with teeth and hair

ww.Immature teratoma: Immature teratoma is a bulky, mostly solid gray-brown mass with hemorrhage and necrosis in a girl or young woman, and its microscopy shows immature neuroepithelium. Teeth and hair in a mature skin-lined nodule mean a benign dermoid.
ww.Endometrioma (chocolate cyst): An endometrioma is a cyst filled with thick, dark brown fluid from old blood and lined by endometrial tissue. It holds no teeth, hair or sebaceous material, the signature of a dermoid.
ww.Mucinous cystadenoma: A mucinous cystadenoma is a large, smooth, multiloculated cyst filled with sticky, glossy mucin and lined by tall mucus-secreting cells. It does not contain skin, hair or teeth.
ww.Ovarian fibroma: An ovarian fibroma is a solid, firm, white-tan tumor with a whorled cut surface and no cysts, teeth or hair. It makes no hormone but can cause Meigs syndrome, with ascites and a pleural effusion.

look: Several well-formed teeth and a tuft of hair are packed into one specimen with yellow, greasy-looking tissue. A teratoma holds tissue from all three germ layers, so skin, hair, sebum and teeth are typical, and in a young woman it is almost always benign. A dermoid is also a classic cause of ovarian torsion, because its weight makes the ovary swing on its stalk.

findings: Teeth: several well-formed teeth with white enamel crowns project from the specimen, proof that tissue from more than one germ layer has differentiated inside this ovarian germ cell tumor.
Hair: a tuft of fine hairs grows from skin-like tissue at the left, because the lining of a dermoid contains skin with hair follicles and sebaceous glands.
Tooth-bearing nodule: the teeth are embedded in a thick, solid piece of the cyst wall, the Rokitansky nodule, where bone, teeth and most solid tissue of a dermoid concentrate.
